answer_1.quote: The automatic generation of radiology reports from chest X-ray images has seen rapid progress with the advent of advanced generative AI technologies.

answer_2.quote: Current metrics for evaluating chest X-ray report generation fall into four main categories: overlap-based, embedding-based, named entity recognition (NER)-based, and large language model (LLM)-based approaches.

answer_3.quote: To identify and classify errors between reference and candidate reports, we used Gemini 2.5 Pro 03-25 preview version deployed via Vertex AI on Google Cloud.
methods: error analysis using LLM with structured prompt
criteria: Incorrect location or position of finding
Mention of comparison not present in the reference impression
Omission of comparison describing a change from a previous study

answer_4.quote: We evaluated CREPE on four publicly available datasets containing radiologist-annotated errors: ReXVal, ReFiSco-v0, and RaTE-Eval.
answer_4.guideline: For each candidate report, determine: -The count of clinically significant errors. -The count of clinically insignificant errors. Errors can fall into one of these categories: a) False report of a finding in the candidate. b) Missing a finding present in the reference. c) Misidentification of a finding's anatomic location/position. d) Misassessment of the severity of a finding. e) Mentioning a comparison that isn't in the reference. f) Omitting a comparison detailing a change from a prior study.
criteria: Incorrect location or position of finding
Mention of comparison not present in the reference impression
Omission of comparison describing a change from a previous study
